title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (this page and the previous one): A is a Dedekind ring with fraction field K. A 'Dedekind-Azumaya category' C over A is an A-linear category equivalent to the category of projective modules over an Azumaya A-algebra σ. The previous page gives a 2-functor Brd → D, σ ↦ C_σ, which is a 2-equivalence but has no natural inverse. To get an intrinsic invariant, Grothendieck attaches to C the fibred category of 'banalisations' (splittings). Ban(C)(T) consists of the A-linear functors φ: C → Mod(O_T) such that, for some (equivalently any) X, φ(X) is a splitting module of σ = End(X), meaning σ⊗O_T ≅ End(φ(X)). Evaluation at X identifies this with the gerbe of splittings of σ. So C defines a G_m-gerbe G on Spec A whose class is the Brauer class of σ, and this does not depend on X.

This page, step by step:

(1) Universal functor (margin N.B.). There is a tautological functor C × G → Mod, i.e. a universal twisted 'fibre functor'.

(2) Fully faithful embedding. This gives a fully faithful functor C → Rep(G). Its essential image is the representations of the gerbe (locally free sheaves on G) that are 'of degree 1' and locally free of a given rank n(x), where n(x) is the locally constant degree function of σ on Spec A. In modern language: modules over an Azumaya algebra are the same as weight-1 (1-twisted) locally free sheaves on the associated G_m-gerbe, of rank n.

(3) Classification. A Dedekind-Azumaya category over A is 'the same as' a G_m-gerbe on S = Spec A together with a locally constant function n(x), such that locally (a condition checkable globally) the gerbe comes from an Azumaya algebra of degree n(x).

(4) Non-Azumaya case. Now let C be a Dedekind category over A: the End(X) are orders, presumably maximal, in central simple K-algebras. Let U ⊂ Spec A be the largest open set on which these orders are Azumaya. On U one gets a gerbe G_U with lien G_m and a class in Br(U). The base change C⊗_A A', with A' = Γ(U), is reinterpreted as the weight-1 representations of G_U, via canonical equivalences defined up to unique isomorphism.

(5) Determinants (margin). For X in C one can define det X as an object of Rep(G): the determinant of a rank-n twisted bundle, i.e. a weight-n twisted line bundle. If X' = P⊗_O X with P an invertible module over O = End(X), there is a canonical isomorphism det X' ≅ det X ⊗ N_red(P). Here N_red is the reduced-norm functor from locally free (invertible) O-modules to invertible A-modules.

Purpose: the next page seeks conditions under which these determinants can be canonically trivialized compatibly. Those conditions are Pic(A) = 0, Φ∩A* = {1} and Φ·A* = K*, with Φ = N_red(E*). They hold for A = Z when E is not split at R. The aim is a canonical invertible object in Rep(G_{A'}) that rigidifies the 'liens structuraux' of the gerbe. This serves the 1965 programme of a Galois theory of motives with integral, non-commutative coefficients: gerbes replace groups when the endomorphism algebras are non-split.
errors: The rank condition should read: locally free of rank n(x), where the Azumaya algebra has rank n(x)^2 (degree n). Grothendieck's phrase 'algèbre d'Azumaya de rang n(x)' is loose about rank versus degree. Not a mathematical error.

'localement ... vérifiable globalement': the condition that the gerbe comes locally from an Azumaya algebra of degree n is local. Over a Dedekind base it holds because Br = Br' for regular schemes of dimension ≤ 1 and period divides index. This is stated without proof.

In step (4), Grothendieck does not say on this page that the orders are maximal or hereditary, which is needed for a good reduced norm on invertible modules. The functor N_red on locally free O-modules is only sketched.

ideas.what: G_m-gerbe of splittings (banalisations) of an Azumaya algebra, defined intrinsically from the linear category C via functors C → Mod(O_T)
ideas.modern_name: Gerbe of trivializations / Brauer class as G_m-gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Le groupe de Brauer I, 1966) and Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971)
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I (Dix exposés), via Giraud's gerbe formalism

ideas.what: Fully faithful functor C → Rep(G) whose image is the degree-1 representations, locally free of rank n
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence between modules over an Azumaya algebra and weight-1 (twisted) locally free sheaves on the associated G_m-gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (1971); popularized by Căldăraru (2000), de Jong, Lieblich (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Probably implicit in Brauer I; explicit in Giraud, Cohomologie non abélienne

ideas.what: Linear categories of Azumaya type classified by a G_m-gerbe plus a locally constant degree function
ideas.modern_name: Brauer 2-category / twisted-sheaf description of Azumaya categories; Tannakian-gerbe viewpoint
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud; Saavedra Rivano (1972) for Tannakian gerbes; Deligne

ideas.what: Determinant of an object of C as a weight-n twisted line bundle on the gerbe, with det(P⊗X) ≅ det X ⊗ N_red(P)
ideas.modern_name: Determinant of twisted sheaves; reduced norm on locally free class groups of orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lieblich (moduli of twisted sheaves, ~2007); Fröhlich/Swan/Reiner for reduced norms of locally free modules

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck explicitly states that modules over an Azumaya algebra are the weight-1 locally free representations of the associated G_m-gerbe, as a fully faithful embedding C → Rep(G) with characterized image. This is the twisted-sheaf dictionary usually attributed to Giraud (1971) and later Căldăraru/Lieblich.
missed.quote: On a de plus un foncteur pleinement fidèle C ⟶ Rep(G) dont l'image est formée des représentations de G qui sont "de degré 1"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only: it dates the twisted-sheaf viewpoint to Grothendieck's motivic Galois notes, earlier than its usual citations.

missed.claim: Programme to use determinants of objects, viewed as twisted line bundles, together with reduced norms of maximal orders, to canonically rigidify the gerbe of a Dedekind category over Z. The intended setting is integral motives with non-split, e.g. definite, endomorphism algebras. The construction stops at conditions on Pic(A) and on N_red(E*).
missed.quote: On peut donc définir det X pour X ∈ ob C comme un objet de Rep(G). Si X' = P⊗_O X, on a alors un iso. canonique det(X') ≃ det(X) N_red(P)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a mildly interesting precursor to integral or arithmetic Tannakian gerbes and determinant rigidifications. Mathematically it is fairly standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a clean early (1965) statement of the Azumaya-modules = weight-1 twisted sheaves equivalence and of determinants of twisted sheaves with reduced norms, in a motivic-Galois context. This is a notable early formulation, but the content is now standard (Giraud, Căldăraru, Lieblich) and was largely in the Grothendieck–Giraud circle.
transcription_corrections: 'U ⊂ Spec S' should read 'U ⊂ Spec A' (S = Spec A).
'C ⊗_A Γ(U)/A'' is C ⊗_A A' with the label A' = Γ(U) written under Γ(U); it is not a quotient.
'Ban_T(C)(T)' on the previous page is presumably 'Ban(C)(T)'.
The image line 'qui sont "de degré 1" et sont localement ... de degré donné n(x)' presumably means locally free of rank n(x).
'Mod.loc.libres(O) → Mod.inv.(A)' is the reduced-norm functor from locally free O-modules to invertible A-modules (margin).
